name: Sylvia's Restaurant
tagline: Harlem's soul food landmark, family run since 1962.
description: Sylvia Woods opened this Lenox Avenue dining room in 1962, and her family still runs it. The menu is Southern soul food, and the restaurant takes reservations.

_verified.note: Black-owned: founded by Sylvia Woods, still family owned (Wikipedia, Free Tours by Foot). Open: own site shows current reservations and an August 2026 hiring post.

name: Melba's
tagline: Melba Wilson's Harlem comfort food spot, known for chicken and waffles.
description: Melba Wilson opened her Harlem restaurant on West 114th Street in 2005. It serves Harlem comfort food, and she added a Grand Central Terminal location in 2025.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Melba Wilson named as owner (Ebony, Michelin Guide Feb 2025). Open: Time Out list updated Feb 2026, Michelin 2025 piece, live reservation page. Phone not found on the pages opened, left null.

name: Red Rooster Harlem
tagline: Marcus Samuelsson's Lenox Avenue restaurant serving Harlem comfort food.
description: Chef Marcus Samuelsson opened Red Rooster on Lenox Avenue in December 2010. It serves comfort food in a Harlem dining room and bar.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Time Out's Black-owned NYC list (updated Feb 2026) names Marcus Samuelsson. Open: live site with 2026 footer and current menu. Price range is an estimate.

name: Sugar Hill Creamery
tagline: Harlem ice cream shop from Petrushka Bazin Larsen and Nick Larsen.
description: Petrushka Bazin Larsen and Nick Larsen started Sugar Hill Creamery in 2017. Their Harlem ice cream shops are on Lenox Avenue and Broadway.

_verified.note: Black-owned: on Time Out's Black-owned NYC list (updated Feb 2026), owners named on own site. Open: live site with both locations listed. Second shop at 3629 Broadway.

name: Ramen By Ra
tagline: Chef Rasheeda Purdie's weekend ramen shop in the East Village.
description: Chef Rasheeda Purdie runs Ramen By Ra from an East Village shop that opened in 2025. It is open Friday to Sunday daytime and takes reservations through Resy.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Time Out's Black-owned NYC list (updated Feb 2026). Open: own site lists Fri to Sun 9am to 4pm hours and a Resy link. Founding year of the brand not stated, left null.

name: Harlem Hops
tagline: Harlem's craft beer bar, opened by three HBCU graduates in 2018.
description: Kevin Bradford, Kim Harris, and Stacey Lee opened Harlem Hops in June 2018 as a craft beer bar on Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard. It pours craft beer and serves food.

_verified.note: Black-owned: HBCU Buzz describes it as 100% African American owned and names the founders. Open: live site with current hours.

name: Charles Pan-Fried Chicken
tagline: Charles Gabriel's pan-fried chicken on West 145th Street in Harlem.
description: Chef Charles Gabriel has been serving pan-fried chicken in New York since 1990. The Harlem shop on West 145th Street is one of three locations.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Time Out's Black-owned NYC list (updated Feb 2026) names chef Charles Gabriel. Open: own site lists three locations, daily hours, and a 2026 footer. Founding year of this flagship not stated, left null.

name: Scarr's Pizza
tagline: Scarr Pimentel's Lower East Side pizza shop.
description: Scarr Pimentel runs this Orchard Street pizza shop selling slices and whole pies. The brand also lists a Las Vegas location.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Time Out's Black-owned NYC list (updated Feb 2026) names Scarr Pimentel. Open: Time Out Feb 2026 plus live site. Site header also mentions Las Vegas, so slug carries -new-york.

name: Hav & Mar
tagline: Marcus Samuelsson's Chelsea seafood restaurant with Ethiopian and Nordic roots.
description: Hav & Mar is Marcus Samuelsson's seafood restaurant in Chelsea, with executive chef Fariyal Abdullahi in the kitchen. The menu pairs Ethiopian ingredients with a Nordic approach.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Time Out's Black-owned NYC list (updated Feb 2026). Open: listed on that Feb 2026 update, live site with reservation form. Phone and opening year not on the pages opened.

name: Ginjan Café
tagline: West African cafe from the Diallo brothers, with ginger juice and jollof bowls.
description: Brothers Mohammed and Rahim Diallo run Ginjan, a West African cafe. It serves ginger and bissap juices and jollof bowls, with spots in Harlem and Bed-Stuy.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Time Out Feb 2025 guide to Black-owned Bed-Stuy features the Ginjan Café there, own site names the Diallo brothers. Open: Time Out Feb 2025 plus live site. Address is the 125th Street one from the site footer; the Brooklyn address was not confirmed.

name: Dept of Culture
tagline: Ayo Balogun's Nigerian tasting menu in Bed-Stuy, BYOB.
description: Chef Ayo Balogun cooks a set menu drawn from north-central Nigeria on Nostrand Avenue. It is BYOB and books through Resy.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black-Owned Brooklyn profile and Resy (Feb 2025) name Ayo Balogun. Open: Resy Feb 2025, Time Out list Feb 2026. Own domain did not resolve, so website left null.

name: Bunna Cafe
tagline: Plant-based Ethiopian cafe in Brooklyn since 2011.
description: Bunna Cafe has served plant-based Ethiopian food on Flushing Avenue since 2011. Liyuwork Ayalew is a co-owner.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Time Out's Black-owned NYC list (updated Feb 2026) and own site. Open: live site with menu and hours.

name: Ras Plant Based
tagline: Ethiopian vegan restaurant in Crown Heights from Romeo and Milka Regalli.
description: Romeo and Milka Regalli serve plant-based Ethiopian food on Franklin Avenue in Crown Heights. The brand runs more than one location, and this is its Brooklyn spot.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Time Out's Black-owned NYC list (updated Feb 2026) and own site name the owners. Open: live location page with hours. Brand has other location pages, so slug carries -brooklyn.

name: Cafe Rue Dix
tagline: Senegalese cafe and bistro on Bedford Avenue in Crown Heights.
description: Lamine Diagne and Nilea Alexander run Cafe Rue Dix, a Senegalese cafe in Crown Heights. It serves Senegalese food and drinks.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Time Out's Black-owned NYC list (updated Feb 2026) names the owners; also profiled by Black-Owned Brooklyn. Open: listed in that Feb 2026 update, live site.

name: Je T'aime Patisserie
tagline: Jatee Kearsley's French bakery in Bed-Stuy, known for croissants.
description: Jatee Kearsley opened this French bakery on Marcus Garvey Boulevard in 2023. It is known for croissants.

_verified.note: Black-owned: ABC7 and BK Reader name owner Jatee Kearsley. Open: Time Out list updated Feb 2026. Own domain did not resolve, so website left null.

name: Kokomo
tagline: Pan-Caribbean restaurant in Williamsburg from Ria and Kevol Graham.
description: Ria and Kevol Graham opened Kokomo on Kent Avenue in 2020. The menu is pan-Caribbean, and reservations are taken through SevenRooms.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black-Owned Brooklyn profile names the Grahams. Open: own site has 2026 footer, current hours, and SevenRooms booking; on Time Out Feb 2026. Site lists two different phone numbers, so phone left null. Price range is an estimate.

name: A&A Bake and Doubles
tagline: Trinidadian doubles shop on Fulton Street, a James Beard America's Classic.
description: A&A serves Trinidadian doubles, goat roti, and shrimp bakes on Fulton Street in Bed-Stuy. It won a James Beard America's Classics award in 2019.

_verified.note: Black-owned: listed in Time Out's Black-owned NYC list (Feb 2026) and its Black-owned Bed-Stuy guide (Feb 2025). Open: both dated Time Out pieces. Owner names and website not confirmed, left null.

name: The Nourish Spot
tagline: Jamaica, Queens health food spot for smoothies, salads, and protein waffles.
description: Dawn Kelly founded The Nourish Spot on Guy R. Brewer Boulevard in Jamaica, Queens. It serves smoothies, salads, and protein waffles.

_verified.note: Black-owned: CBS New York (June 2021) Black Restaurant Week feature on founder Dawn Kelly; BuyBlack list (Mar 2025). Open: BuyBlack Mar 2025 is the most recent dated source; own site refused the connection, so website left null. Worth a quick recheck.

name: The Lit. Bar
tagline: Noëlle Santos's Mott Haven bookstore and wine bar.
description: Noëlle Santos opened The Lit. Bar on Alexander Avenue in Mott Haven in 2019. It is a bookstore and wine bar that hosts author events.

_verified.note: Black-owned: NYC Tourism Black-owned bookstores article (updated Jan 2026) and Wikipedia name Noëlle Santos. Open: NYC Tourism Jan 2026 update, NYT coverage Nov 2024 cited on Wikipedia. Own site returned errors when fetched, so website left null.

name: Sister's Uptown Bookstore
tagline: Washington Heights bookstore and cultural center focused on Black authors since 2000.
description: Janifer P. Wilson founded Sister's Uptown in 2000 and runs it with her daughter Kori Wilson. The shop stocks books by Black authors and hosts readings, talks, and community events.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Amsterdam News (July 2025) and NYC Tourism (Jan 2026). Open: own site lists fall 2026 events, including an Oct 24 gala. The store ran a fundraiser in 2025 to stay open.

name: Café con Libros
tagline: Feminist bookstore and coffee shop in Crown Heights.
description: Kalima DeSuze runs Café con Libros, an Afro-Latine, woman and veteran owned feminist bookstore and coffee shop on Prospect Place. It sells books and hosts community events.

_verified.note: Black-owned: NYC Tourism Black-owned bookstores article (updated Jan 2026); own site says Afro-Latine woman and veteran owned. Open: own site lists Sept to Dec 2026 pre-orders. Opening year not confirmed, left null.

name: The Studio Museum in Harlem
tagline: Museum for artists of African descent, reopened in a new 125th Street building in 2025.
description: The Studio Museum in Harlem shows work by artists of African descent and runs its well-known artist in residence program. Its new building on West 125th Street opened in November 2025, with pay what you can admission and free Sundays.

_verified.note: Black-led institution devoted to artists of African descent (own press page, Museums Association Nov 2025). Open: reopened Nov 15, 2025; visit page lists Wed to Sun hours. Founding year not on the pages opened.

name: Weeksville Heritage Center
tagline: Historic site preserving Weeksville, a free Black community founded in the 1830s.
description: Weeksville Heritage Center in Crown Heights preserves the Hunterfly Road houses of Weeksville, one of the country's largest free Black communities before the Civil War. It offers tours, exhibitions, and events, and admission is free.

_verified.note: Black-led cultural institution devoted to Black history (own site). Open: visit page lists Tue to Sat hours; Brooklyn Community Foundation and PIX11 coverage of a March 2026 grant. Founding year not stated on the pages opened.

name: Dance Theatre of Harlem
tagline: The first Black classical ballet company, founded in Harlem in 1969.
description: Arthur Mitchell, Brock Peters, and Cicely Tyson founded Dance Theatre of Harlem in 1969 to bring classical ballet training to Harlem's children. The company still performs and runs its school on West 152nd Street, under artistic director Robert Garland.

_verified.note: Black-led: Wikipedia calls it the first Black classical ballet company and names its founders. Open: own site has a 2026 footer and promotes its 2027 New York season and summer intensives. Zip and phone not on the pages opened.

name: Museum of Contemporary African Diasporan Arts (MoCADA)
tagline: Fort Greene museum for art and culture of Africa and its diaspora.
description: Laurie Cumbo founded MoCADA in 1999 to present art and culture of Africa and its diaspora. It runs exhibitions, events, and walking tours from 10 Lafayette Avenue.

_verified.note: Black-founded cultural institution (Wikipedia names founder Laurie Cumbo). Open: own site lists October and November 2026 tours and an Oct 20, 2026 event. The Ubuntu Garden is closed for renovation, and the old Hanson Place site closed in 2024.

name: The Billie Holiday Theatre
tagline: Restoration Plaza theater staging Black stories in Bed-Stuy since 1972.
description: The Billie Holiday Theatre has staged work about the African diaspora experience at Restoration Plaza since 1972. It produces plays, runs residencies and education programs, and received the National Medal of Arts in 2023.

_verified.note: Black-led institution: own site centers Black stories and culture; Wikipedia notes its African diaspora mission. Open: live site promoting a spring production and its Legacy Forward Awards gala, no dated show list found.

name: Silvana
tagline: Harlem cafe by day, live music and DJ room downstairs at night.
description: Silvana is a cafe on West 116th Street with a downstairs room for live music and DJ nights. Its owners also run Shrine World Music Venue and Yatenga in Harlem.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Time Out's Black-owned NYC list (updated Feb 2026). Open: own site has a music calendar with shows on Oct 15 to 24, 2026 and beyond. Owners are not named on the pages opened.

name: Boogie Down Bronx Honey
tagline: Raw honey from beehives kept across the Bronx and Manhattan.
description: The Flynn family keeps beehives around the Bronx and Manhattan and sells the raw honey online. They also run community harvest days at local gardens.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black Farmers Index NY listing. Open: own site has an online shop and a September 2025 community harvest at KHCC Garden. Service area, no public storefront.

name: Hattie Carthan Herban Farm
tagline: Bed-Stuy community farm collecting chemical-free produce from local growers.
description: Hattie Carthan Herban Farm in Bed-Stuy, led by Yonnette Fleming, grows and collects chemical-free produce from neighborhood gardeners. It has also run a community farmers market.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black Farmers Index NY listing; Civil Eats profile of Yonnette Fleming. Draft because no 2024 to 2026 activity was found, and the market website listed in the index no longer resolves.

name: Carver Federal Savings Bank
tagline: Harlem-based Black-owned community bank, serving New York since 1948.
description: Carver is a Black-owned community bank headquartered on West 125th Street in Harlem. It has branches in Harlem, Brooklyn, and St. Albans, Queens, and focuses on lending in underserved neighborhoods.

_verified.note: Black-owned: National Bankers Association / CDBA profile describes Carver as a Black-owned bank. Open: Carver rang the Nasdaq bell for Juneteenth in June 2025; locations page lists six branches. Address is the corporate headquarters; founded_year 1948 is from the own site's since 1948 line.

name: Moshood Creations
tagline: Designer Moshood's Bed-Stuy boutique for West African prints and streetwear.
description: Nigerian-born designer Moshood has run his Brooklyn boutique for more than two decades. It sells West African print clothing alongside streetwear.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black-Owned Brooklyn profile of the Nigerian-born owner. Open: own site lists daily hours, current products, and a 2026 footer. Moved from Fort Greene to 1360 Fulton St (Bed-Stuy). Founding year not stated, left null.

name: Byas & Leon
tagline: Tompkins Avenue shop for vintage, Black-owned brands, and shirts sewn in Haiti.
description: Rony Byas and Harvey Leon sell vintage clothing alongside fair-trade and independent Black-owned brands. Their own button-down shirts are hand cut and sewn in Haiti.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black-Owned Brooklyn profile and Time Out Black-owned Bed-Stuy guide (Feb 2025). Open: own site lists Fri to Sun hours and a 2026 footer. 2013 is when the clothing line launched; the store opened in 2019.

name: Browstress
tagline: DUMBO studio for microblading, lip blush, and freckle tattoos.
description: Krystal Cummings opened Browstress in 2018 and now runs it from Jay Street in DUMBO. The studio does microblading, brow shading, lip blushing, and freckle tattoos, and teaches beginner courses.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black-Owned Brooklyn profile of Krystal Cummings. Open: own site has live booking, academy courses, and a 2026 footer. Price range is an estimate.

name: Papa Rozier Farms
tagline: Castor and moringa oils grown in Haiti and made into body care in Brooklyn.
description: Papa Rozier Farms grows moringa and castor in Haiti and turns the oils into body and hair care in Brooklyn. Products are sold online and from its Flushing Avenue farmhouse.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black Farmers Index NY listing; also profiled by Black-Owned Brooklyn as an all-natural beauty boutique. Open: own shop live with a 2026 footer. Owner and founding year not stated on the pages opened.

name: De Lux Gallery
tagline: Fort Greene natural hair and loc salon.
description: Glen Ettienne opened De Lux Gallery on Fulton Street in Fort Greene in 2006. The salon focuses on natural hair, including locs.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black-Owned Brooklyn profile of Glen Ettienne. Draft because no dated 2024 to 2026 activity was confirmed and no website was found.

name: Life Wellness Center
tagline: Bed-Stuy acupuncture, massage, and herbal apothecary on Tompkins Avenue.
description: Khadijah Tudor and Ade Collman opened Life Wellness Center in 2016. It offers massage and acupuncture, plus an apothecary.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black-Owned Brooklyn profile names the owners. Open: own site lists current weekly hours and online booking; its footer says 2024 and no newer date was found.

name: Good Wine
tagline: Park Slope wine shop that carries bottles from Black winemakers.
description: Heather Johnston took over this Fifth Avenue wine shop in 2015 and renamed it Good Wine. The shop carries bottles from Black winemakers.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black-Owned Brooklyn profile of Heather Johnston. Draft because the website loads but shows no content, and no dated 2024 to 2026 activity was found.

name: peace & RIOT
tagline: Tompkins Avenue gift shop for books, candles, kitchenware, and art.
description: peace & RIOT is a Bed-Stuy gift shop selling books, candles, kitchenware, and art. It also sells online.

_verified.note: Black-owned: included in Time Out's Black-owned Bed-Stuy guide (Feb 2025); owner not named. Open: own shop live with a 2026 footer. Site lists 401 to 405 Tompkins Ave.

name: The Narativ House
tagline: Bed-Stuy shop and cafe for clothing, home decor, and books.
description: Ayo Agbede and Farai Simoyi run The Narativ House, which shares a Tompkins Avenue space with the Brooklyn Kettle cafe. It sells clothing, home decor, and books.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black-Owned Brooklyn profile names the owners. Open: own shop lists Tue to Sun hours and current products, though no dated 2025 or 2026 item was found.
